How to use this calculator

  1. Enter text to read, reading speed.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How reading time is calculated

Reading time gives readers a useful planning estimate, especially for newsletters and longer articles. Words are counted as groups of characters separated by whitespace. Adjust the reading speed rather than treating a single average as universal. A reader scanning familiar material may move quickly; a reader checking equations or learning a new subject needs more time. This estimate excludes time spent interpreting charts or following links.

Reading time in minutes = number of words ÷ words per minute
A worked example

A 900-word article at 225 words per minute takes about four minutes. At a careful pace of 150 words per minute, allow six minutes.

Assumptions & useful context

This is a whitespace-based word estimate. Technical material, images and unfamiliar language can take longer.

Frequently asked questions

Is this a prediction of my actual reading speed?

No. It applies the speed you enter to a simple word count. Your actual pace varies with the subject and purpose.

Is my text uploaded?

No. Counting happens in your browser. Avoid adding the text to a share link if you do not want it in the URL.
